question: Obtain the vector equation of the line passing through $A(2,-1,4)$ and $B(-1,5,0)$.
explanation: Step 1: The position vector of $A(2,-1,4)$ is $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$. Step 2: The direction of the required line is obtained from $\overrightarrow{AB}$. Its components are $(-1-2,5-(-1),0-4)=(-3,6,-4)$. Thus, $$\overrightarrow{AB}=-3\hat{i}+6\hat{j}-4\hat{k}.$$ Step 3: A line passing through a point with position vector $\vec{a}$ and parallel to a vector $\vec{b}$ has equation $\vec{r}=\vec{a}+\lambda\vec{b}$. Step 4: Substituting the obtained vectors, $$\vec{r}=(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k})+\lambda(-3\hat{i}+6\hat{j}-4\hat{k}),\quad \lambda\in\mathbb{R}.$$ Step 5: Hence, this is the required vector equation of the line through $A$ and $B$.
